description: Step-5 third-person-singular subject-verb agreement (audit commit ad3641395), rule en-step5-subject-verb-agreement. A He/She/It subject directly followed by a base verb in {go, make, work} is conjugated (go->goes, make->makes, work->works), but only when the sentence is not question-like and carries no SVA temporal blocker. expectedStatus/expectedCorrection are the VERIFIED output of correctWithTutorRules('en') on current main (captured from the live engine).
fp_risk_note: Medium overlap risk. This rule runs before the third-person daily/school-routine rules and preempts the bare 'He go ...' case, so 'go' positives here are real (e.g. 'She go to the park'). make/work are unique to this rule and isolate it unambiguously. Guards stressed by the negatives: (1) already-conjugated input ('He goes to work') must not double-fire; (2) an SVA temporal blocker ('yesterday', and also on-weekday/in-year/season/N-hours-ago) suppresses this rule — locked here with 'yesterday'; (3) question-like input ('Does he go to work?') is excluded; (4) non He/She/It subjects ('I go to work') are correct English. Note: with a non-yesterday blocker + 'go to school', the routine rule (not this one) fires instead — see third-person-school-routine fixtures.

positive.notes: make -> makes; 'make' is unique to this rule, so it isolates cleanly.
go -> goes; this rule preempts the third-person daily/school rules for the bare 'go' case (not 'to school', no 'every day').

negative.notes: Already correctly conjugated — must not double-fire.
FP-stress (temporal blocker): 'yesterday' (an SVA temporal blocker) suppresses this rule; the verb is already past anyway.
FP-stress (question): question-like input is excluded; 'does ...' already carries the agreement.
First-person subject is correct English; the rule is He/She/It only.
Confusable: intervening adverb 'always' breaks the 'He + verb' adjacency, so the rule abstains.

negative.input: He, I think, go to work.
negative.expectedCorrection: He, I think, go to work.
negative.notes: Confusable: parenthetical between subject and verb breaks adjacency, so the rule abstains.
